docs.title: About HUI-MY Docs Hub
docs.text:
HUI-MY Docs Hub is the central documentation portal for the HUI-MY ecosystem. It gathers links, guides, and references for all HUI-MY projects — from computational biology tools to high‑performance computing libraries — into one organized place.

Whether you are looking for installation instructions, API references, or step‑by‑step tutorials, this portal helps you find the right documentation quickly.

docs.title: What is HUI-MY?
docs.text:
HUI-MY is a personal‑driven computational biology laboratory focusing on:

  • Enzyme engineering and rational protein design
  • Molecular simulation and virtual screening
  • High‑performance computing with C++/CUDA
  • Computational chemistry and machine learning integration

We not only use existing software but also build reusable underlying infrastructure for computational biology. Our goal is to lower the barrier to entry by openly sharing knowledge, code, and tools.

docs.title: What You’ll Find Here
docs.text: The portal organizes documentation into several categories:

docs.title: Tools Documentation
docs.text: Detailed guides for self‑developed tools and frameworks, including installation, usage, and examples. Examples: Protein Phaser, BioCUDA, Vina‑CUDA, FlexTrimmer, and more.

docs.title: Tutorials & Guides
docs.text: Step‑by‑step tutorials covering common workflows, from getting started to advanced analysis pipelines. Examples: Getting Started with HUI‑MY Tools, Workflow Examples, Molecular Dynamics Theory.

docs.title: API References
docs.text: Programmatic access documentation for REST APIs and Python SDKs where available.

docs.title: Community & Support
docs.text: Links to forums, blogs, and main site for discussions, updates, and further help.

docs.title: HUI-MY Ecosystem
docs.text:
This portal is part of the larger HUI-MY digital platform:

Site Purpose Main Site Portal and introduction Lab Computational biology research and experiments Blog Thoughts, tutorials, and technical notes Forum Discussion, support, and collaboration Docs (this site) Project documentation and learning resources

docs.title: Open Source & Sharing
docs.text: HUI-MY is committed to open source and knowledge sharing. Most tools and scripts are publicly available on GitHub. We believe that open collaboration accelerates scientific progress and helps everyone learn faster.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
If you have questions, suggestions, or need further assistance, feel free to reach out:

  • Email: suguohui_account@163.com
  • Forum: comm.huimy.top
  • GitHub: GuiHui-huimy

Thank you for visiting HUI-MY Docs Hub!

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
This chapter explains how to contribute to the LabPress project. It covers reporting issues, proposing changes, setting up a development environment, following code conventions, and submitting pull requests.

The goal is to make the contribution process clear and predictable while maintaining the quality and consistency of the project.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
LabPress is an open-source project released under the GNU General Public License v3.0. Contributions are welcome from anyone, including bug reports, feature suggestions, documentation improvements, and code changes.

The project is hosted on GitHub:

https://github.com/GuiHui-huimy/LabPress

All contributions should be submitted through GitHub Issues and Pull Requests.

docs.title: 2. Code of Conduct
docs.text:
All contributors are expected to follow the project’s Code of Conduct. The full text is available in the CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md file in the repository root.

The Code of Conduct establishes basic expectations for respectful communication and professional behavior. Please read it before participating in discussions or submitting contributions.

docs.title: 3. Reporting Issues
docs.text: Issues are used to report bugs, request features, or suggest improvements.

docs.title: 3.1 Bug Reports
docs.text:
When reporting a bug, include as much relevant information as possible:

  • LabPress version or commit hash.
  • PHP version and MySQL version.
  • Web server and hosting environment, if relevant.
  • Steps to reproduce the problem.
  • Expected behavior and actual behavior.
  • Any relevant error messages or screenshots.

A clear bug report helps maintainers understand and fix the problem faster.

docs.title: 3.2 Feature Requests
docs.text:
Feature requests should describe the problem that the feature would solve rather than only the desired solution. Include:

  • The use case or scenario.
  • Why the current behavior is insufficient.
  • How the proposed change would improve the system.
  • Any relevant examples or references.

docs.title: 3.3 Security Issues
docs.text: Do not report security vulnerabilities through public issues. Instead, follow the process described in SECURITY.md. Security reports are handled privately until a fix is ready.

docs.title: 4. Development Setup
docs.text: Contributors who want to make code changes should set up a local development environment.

docs.title: 4.1 Requirements
docs.text:
Ensure the following are installed:

  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • MySQL 5.7+ or MariaDB 10.3+
  • PHP extensions: pdo, pdo_mysql, json, mbstring, session, fileinfo, zip
  • Git

docs.title: 4.2 Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/GuiHui-huimy/LabPress.git
cd LabPress

docs.title: 4.3 Create a Local Database
docs.text:
mysql -u root -p -e "CREATE DATABASE labpress_dev CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci;"
mysql -u root -p labpress_dev < labpressexample.sql

docs.title: 4.4 Configure the Database Connection
docs.text:
Edit includes/config.php and set the database credentials for the local environment.

Keep the local configuration private. Do not commit changes to config.php if they contain real credentials.

docs.title: 4.5 Start the Local Server
docs.text:
Use the PHP built-in server:

php -S 127.0.0.1:8080

Then open:

http://127.0.0.1:8080

The admin panel is available at:

http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin

Default administrator credentials are provided by the sample database. Change them after first login.

docs.title: 5. Branching and Workflow
docs.text: Contributions should be made through feature branches and pull requests.

docs.title: 5.1 Fork the Repository
docs.text: If you do not have write access to the main repository, create a fork on GitHub and clone your fork.

docs.title: 5.2 Create a Feature Branch
docs.text:
Use a short, descriptive branch name:

git checkout -b fix-news-permission

Examples:

  • fix-upload-validation
  • add-plugin-hook
  • update-readme

docs.title: 5.3 Make Focused Changes
docs.text: Keep each pull request focused on one change or one logical group of changes. Avoid mixing unrelated modifications in the same branch.

docs.title: 5.4 Commit Messages
docs.text:
Use clear and descriptive commit messages. The first line should summarize the change. If necessary, add a blank line followed by a more detailed explanation.

Example:

Fix permission check in user management API

The PUT method now verifies that only users with the all
permission can modify other users. Self-service password
changes remain available for all authenticated users.

docs.title: 6. Code Standards
docs.text: LabPress is written in plain PHP, JavaScript, and CSS without external frameworks. Contributors should follow the existing style conventions.

docs.title: 6.1 PHP
docs.text:
• Use prepared statements for all database queries.
  • Escape output with htmlspecialchars() where user-visible data is rendered.
  • Use the short array syntax [].
  • Prefer clear function names and avoid abbreviations unless they are obvious.
  • Follow the existing code organization, placing shared functions in includes/functions.php and admin views in admin/views/.
  • Do not add third-party PHP dependencies unless absolutely necessary.

docs.title: 6.2 JavaScript
docs.text:
• Use plain JavaScript without framework dependencies.
  • Keep admin JavaScript files in admin/assets/js/ and frontend JavaScript in assets/js/.
  • Use descriptive variable names and avoid polluting the global namespace unless consistent with existing code.

docs.title: 6.3 CSS
docs.text:
• Follow the existing pattern of page-specific stylesheets.
  • Use CSS variables where the current theme supports them.
  • Avoid inline styles in templates unless the style is generated dynamically.

docs.title: 6.4 Language Files
docs.text:
When adding new interface strings:

  • Add the key to all existing language files.
  • Use descriptive keys and consistent naming.
  • For plugin language files, use a unique prefix to avoid conflicts with core keys.

docs.title: 6.5 Database Changes
docs.text:
If a change requires a new table or column:

  • Update the labpressexample.sql file so that new installations include the change.
  • Document the change in the relevant documentation page.
  • For plugin-specific tables, prefer creating tables during plugin activation rather than modifying the core SQL dump.

docs.title: 7. Testing
docs.text: Before submitting a pull request, perform basic testing.

docs.title: 7.1 Syntax Checks
docs.text:
Run PHP syntax checks on all changed files:

php -l path/to/changed-file.php

To check all PHP files:

find . -name "*.php" -exec php -l {} \;

docs.title: 7.2 Manual Testing
docs.text:
Manually verify the affected functionality. For example:

  • If the change affects login, test login and logout.
  • If the change affects content management, test creating and editing the relevant content type.
  • If the change affects plugins, test activation, deactivation, and uninstallation.
  • If the change affects translations, test both the admin and frontend language contexts.

docs.title: 7.3 No Automated Test Suite
docs.text: The project does not currently have a formal automated test suite. Manual testing is therefore the primary verification method for contributions.

docs.title: 8. Documentation
docs.text:
Documentation is an important part of the project. When adding or changing features, update the relevant documentation pages under docs/.

Documentation changes can be submitted as pull requests independently of code changes.

When writing documentation:

  • Use clear, concise English.
  • Follow the existing chapter and section structure.
  • Include code examples and screenshots where appropriate.
  • Keep technical descriptions accurate and aligned with the actual implementation.

docs.title: 9. Pull Requests
docs.text: Once your changes are ready, submit a pull request to the main repository.

docs.title: 9.1 Pull Request Checklist
docs.text:
Before submitting:

  • Ensure the branch is up to date with the main branch.
  • Run PHP syntax checks.
  • Test the change manually.
  • Update related documentation if necessary.
  • Avoid committing config.php with real credentials.
  • Do not include unrelated changes in the same pull request.

docs.title: 9.2 Pull Request Description
docs.text:
In the pull request description, explain:

  • What the change does.
  • Why the change is needed.
  • How the change was tested.
  • Any potential side effects or areas that need review.

docs.title: 9.3 Review Process
docs.text:
Maintainers will review the pull request and may request changes. After approval, the changes will be merged into the main branch.

Response times may vary. Keep the discussion professional and focused on the technical content.

docs.title: 10. License
docs.text:
By contributing to LabPress, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the same open-source license as the project. The project is released under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

See the LICENSE file for the full license text.

docs.title: 11. Next Steps
docs.text:
After reading this guide, you may want to:

  • Review the Developer Resources chapter for more detailed technical context.
  • Read the Plugin Development section if you plan to build a plugin.
  • Check the Hooks Reference before adding new hook-related functionality.
  • Explore the API Reference and Database Schema for technical details.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
This chapter describes the security measures implemented in LabPress and provides recommendations for running a LabPress site securely in production. It also explains how to report security vulnerabilities.

The information is intended for site administrators and developers. It covers the built-in protections, deployment considerations, and the process for responsible disclosure.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
LabPress includes several security controls that are designed to protect the application, its data, and its users during normal operation. These controls cover authentication, authorization, database access, output escaping, file uploads, and plugin management.

While LabPress includes these protections, no web application can be considered completely secure without a properly configured hosting environment. Administrators should follow the deployment recommendations in this chapter and keep the system up to date.

docs.title: 2.1 Password Storage
docs.text:
User passwords are never stored in plain text. LabPress uses PHP’s password_hash() function with the bcrypt algorithm to generate password hashes.

During login, the system verifies the supplied password with password_verify(). This ensures that passwords are stored in a format that is resistant to brute-force and precomputation attacks if the database is compromised.

docs.title: 2.2 Session-Based Authentication
docs.text:
Access to the admin panel is protected by PHP sessions. After a successful login, the user’s identity and permissions are stored in session variables.

All admin entry points verify that a valid session exists before allowing access. If the session is missing or invalid, the user is redirected to the login page or the API returns an authentication error.

The admin login process also supports a login_redirect_url filter, but authentication itself is enforced before any admin view is rendered.

docs.title: 2.3 Permission System
docs.text:
LabPress uses a role-based permission model for backend operations.

Each administrator account has a permissions field stored as a JSON array. Permissions are checked before:

  • Rendering admin pages.
  • Executing write operations through the API.
  • Performing sensitive actions such as plugin management, user management, and site configuration.

The hasPermission() function enforces these checks. Users with the all permission have full access. Other permissions allow only the corresponding module access.

docs.title: 2.4 Database Security
docs.text:
All database queries use PDO prepared statements with parameter binding. This prevents SQL injection by separating SQL logic from user-supplied values.

The database connection is configured with:

  • PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION
  • PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false

These settings ensure that errors are handled consistently and that prepared statements are not emulated in a way that could weaken their safety.

docs.title: 2.5 Output Escaping
docs.text:
User-generated content and data retrieved from the database are escaped before being rendered in HTML output.

The templates use htmlspecialchars() to escape dynamic values. This reduces the risk of cross-site scripting (XSS) when displaying content such as news titles, project names, menu items, and configuration values.

Markdown rendering is performed by the bundled Parsedown library, and the resulting HTML is filtered before it is passed to the template layer.

docs.title: 2.6 File Upload Restrictions
docs.text:
The image upload endpoint api/upload.php accepts only a defined set of image MIME types:

  • image/jpeg
  • image/png
  • image/gif
  • image/webp

Uploaded files are saved in the uploads/ directory under a subdirectory determined by the content type. The upload operation is restricted to authenticated users.

Plugin ZIP uploads are restricted to users with the all permission, and the installation process checks for the presence of a plugin.php file inside the uploaded archive.

docs.title: 2.7 Plugin Management Controls
docs.text:
Plugin management actions are restricted to users with the all permission. These actions include:

  • Plugin installation from ZIP
  • Plugin installation from a remote URL
  • Plugin activation and deactivation
  • Plugin uninstallation

The plugin uninstall process validates the plugin slug using a strict pattern that only permits letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. This prevents path traversal through the plugin identifier.

docs.title: 2.8 Configuration Protection
docs.text:
The database configuration file includes/config.php contains sensitive credentials. It is not intended to be committed to version control.

The repository includes a .gitignore rule that excludes config.php. Administrators should verify that this file is not exposed publicly and that the web server is configured to deny direct access to PHP files inside the includes/ directory.

docs.title: 3.1 Use HTTPS
docs.text:
Enable HTTPS on the production server. HTTPS encrypts traffic between the browser and the server, protecting login credentials and session cookies from interception.

Most hosting panels, including BaoTa, provide tools for obtaining and installing free SSL certificates.

docs.title: 3.2 Change Default Credentials
docs.text:
The sample database includes a default administrator account. The credentials are publicly documented and must be changed immediately after installation.

Administrators should create strong, unique passwords and avoid reusing passwords across systems.

docs.title: 3.3 Restrict Access to Sensitive Directories
docs.text:
The following directories should not be publicly accessible through the web server:

  • includes/
  • plugins/ – except through the normal PHP loading process
  • api/ – if direct access is not required, restrict it to application-level routing

The web server should be configured to deny direct access to PHP files in these directories when appropriate.

docs.title: 3.4 Set Correct File Permissions
docs.text:
Directories that require write access from the PHP process should be configured with the minimum necessary permissions.

Typical recommended permissions:

chmod -R 755 uploads/
chmod -R 755 plugins/
chmod -R 755 images/

If the web server runs under a separate user such as www-data, ownership should be adjusted accordingly.

docs.title: 3.5 Keep the System Updated
docs.text:
Check the GitHub repository regularly for new releases and security updates. Apply updates in a timely manner.

Before performing an update, back up the database and the web directory. If the update requires manual file replacement, follow the release notes carefully.

docs.title: 3.6 Backup Regularly
docs.text:
Maintain regular backups of both the database and the uploads/ directory. Backups should be stored in a secure location outside the web root.

The most important data is stored in the MySQL database. Use the backup tools provided by your hosting panel or automated scripts to create periodic database dumps.

docs.title: 3.7 Use Trusted Plugins Only
docs.text:
Plugins can execute PHP code and therefore have full access to the server environment. Only install plugins from trusted sources.

Before activating a new plugin, review its code or ensure that it comes from a repository or author you trust.

docs.title: 4. Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
If you discover a security vulnerability in LabPress, please report it privately. Do not open a public issue or disclose the details until the maintainers have had a chance to address the problem.

The full reporting process is described in the SECURITY.md file in the repository root.

When reporting a vulnerability, include:

  • A clear description of the vulnerability.
  • The affected version or commit.
  • Steps to reproduce the issue.
  • The potential impact.
  • Any suggested remediation, if available.

The maintainers will acknowledge the report and work with the reporter to validate and address the issue.

docs.title: 5. Known Security Boundaries
docs.text:
LabPress is designed for use by research groups and small laboratory teams. It is not intended to be exposed to untrusted, anonymous user registration or content submission.

The admin panel is restricted to trusted administrators. The public frontend is primarily read-oriented and does not allow public user registration or comment submission by default.

When deploying LabPress in a shared or public environment, treat the admin panel as the primary security boundary and restrict access to it using additional controls such as IP allowlists or VPN access if necessary.

docs.title: 6. Next Steps
docs.text:
After reviewing the security documentation, you may want to:

  • Read the Installation Guide for secure installation steps.
  • Review the Basic Configuration for environment settings.
  • Check the Users Management guide for account and permission best practices.
  • Review the Plugin Management guide for plugin safety.
  • Consult the Developer Resources if you are working with the codebase.
